main_body: A pew seen end-on/side: a tall brown backrest post on the left and a seat block to the right with three red cushion panels stacked vertically, separated by tan bands. It reads as a flat side/front elevation.
top_band: At x=8 rows 14-15 (2 rows, tan #b77246) sit directly on the outline, then red panels. This 2px band is only a rim, and no horizontal surface is visible from above.
evidence: The column scan at x=8 shows a 2-row tan band (rows 14-15), then red panels (rows 16-26, 30-40, 44-54) separated by 2-row tan bands. These are vertical faces stacked down the object. There is no seat surface seen from above, and the lighter bands are thin 2px strips. The backrest post on the left is a flat vertical strip. The whole piece is an elevation with a thin rim, so it fails the seat contract that requires the seat surface to be seen from above.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 8 distinct colours and a median of 6 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. Flat-fill coverage is 25% versus 13% and 0%. The red panels are large flat fills with only a dark right/bottom edge, and the brown post and bands have no grain. The outline is a dark brown tint (2% neutral), which is good, but shading depth and texture are far thinner than the Beodeul pieces.
